question.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2}$ of two nails is drawn from a population. The population has nails of two different lengths, $6\,\text{cm}$ and $\text{12}\,\text{cm},$ distributed in the ratio $3:1.$ Calculate $\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}].$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sequence of random variables representing a random sample of size $n$ drawn from a population with population mean $\mu .$ Then, the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is given by

$$
\overset{―}{X}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{X}_{i}.
$$

Since $\overset{―}{X}$ is an unbiased estimator of $\mu ,$ we have

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu .
$$

We're told that the nails in the population have lengths $6\,\text{cm}$ and $\text{12}\,\text{cm},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $3:1.$ Therefore, to compute the population mean, we can consider a population consisting of $3+1=4$ nails only with the following lengths:

$$
6\,\text{cm},\,6\,\text{cm},\,6\,\text{cm},\,12\,\text{cm}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{4}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(3\cdot 6+12) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(18+12) \\  & =\frac{30}{4} \\  & =7.5\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu =7.5\,\text{cm}.
$$
